'''Ahmad Salahuddin''' (7 July 1937 – 26 November 1996) was an Indian [[Biochemistry|biochemist]] who served as a professor of biochemistry and department chairman (1984–1996) at [[Aligarh Muslim University]] (AMU) Aligarh, India.<ref>AMU Aligarh {{Cite web | url=https://www.amu.ac.in/department/interdisciplinary-biotechnology-unit/list-of-former-chairperson | title=List of Former Chairpersons – Interdisciplinary Biotechnology Unit &#124; AMU }}</ref> He was a Founder Director of Interdisciplinary Biotechnology Unit at AMU in 1984.<ref>{{cite web|title=Interdisciplinary Biotechnology Unit, Aligarh|page=About IBU|url=https://icibu.in/|access-date=21 September 2022|archive-date=22 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220922103650/https://icibu.in/}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Salahuddin was born on 7 July 1937 in [[Jairajpur]], [[Azamgarh]], [[Uttar Pradesh]]. His father, Fazlul Bari, was a teacher at the [[Shibli National College, Azamgarh]] where he received his early education, and he later completed his undergraduate and master's degrees in 1955 and 1957 in chemistry from the [[Aligarh Muslim University]].<ref>Salahuddin (1) Fazlul Bari (2) 7.7.1937..(10) Jairajpur, Azamgarh {{cite web |title=Aligarh Muslim University Alumni Directory|page= S696-698|year=2019|url=https://idoc.pub/documents/aligarh-muslim-university-alumni-directory-1d47kw123yn2}}</ref> Initially as a research student, he took interest in physical chemistry, obtaining his PhD degree in chemistry from [[Aligarh Muslim University]] Aligarh (1962).<ref>{{cite thesis| url=http://hdl.handle.net/10603/57378|title=Physico chemical studies on the interaction of metals and their hydrous oxide sols with proteins| year=1962| department=Department of Chemistry Aligarh Muslim University| degree=Ph.D.| last=Anonymous| first=Salahuddin|hdl=10603/57378 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Polarography of Cadmium TransfusionGelatin Mixtures|journal=Nature|author=Wahid U Malik |author2=Salahuddin|volume=200|page=1204|year=1963|issue=4912 |doi=10.1038/2001204a0 |bibcode=1963Natur.200.1204M |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/2001204a0.pdf
}}</ref>

== Career ==
Salahuddin received his second Ph.D. degree at [[Duke University]], where he worked on his Ph.D. dissertation (1964 to 1968).<ref name="our publications">{{cite journal|author=Ahmad Salahuddin and Charles Tanford|title=Thermodynamics of the denaturation of ribonuclease by guanidine hydrochloride|journal=Biochemistry |volume=9|issue=6|pages=1342–1347|year=1970|doi=10.1021/bi00808a007|pmid=5461481 }}</ref> In the laboratory of [[Charles Tanford]], Department of Biochemistry, Duke University, he focussed on the process of protein folding in denaturants with native and the unfolded protein characterizations.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Anfinsen CB | title=Principles that govern the folding of protein chains | journal=Science | volume=181 |issue=4096 |year=1973 | pages=223–230 | pmid=4124164 | doi=10.1126/science.181.4096.223| bibcode=1973Sci...181..223A }}</ref> His early collaborative work in uncovering residual native [[protein structure]], following treatment with heat, acid (low pH) experimentally in a number of model proteins in his lab was published, 1967.<ref>Evidence for residual structure in acid and heat denatured proteins, by Aune, KC, Salahuddin A, Zarlingo, MH and Tanford C. Department of Biochemistry, Duke University Medical Centre NC 27706 USA
https://web.archive.org/web/20190712182255/http://www.jbc.org/content/242/19/4486.full.pdf</ref> He actually performed [[equilibrium unfolding]] studies on [[ribonuclease]] protein in [[guanidine hydrochloride]], the results of which constituted his Ph.D. dissertation required for a Ph.D. degree in biochemistry, Duke University (1968), together with a publication (1970).<ref name="our publications"/>

Salahuddin returned to AMU Aligarh and joined the Department of Biochemistry, Faculty of Medicine, J.N. Medical College as a reader, 1968.<ref name=" our publications"/><ref>Ahmad Salahuddin 1969-72 {{cite web |url=https://www.amu.ac.in/department/bio-chemistry-jnmc/list-of-former-chairperson |title=List of Former Chairpersons- Department of BiochemistryJNMC, AMU}} retrieved 1 Augus2023</ref> Salahuddin was present at the foundation ceremony of the new IBU Building on 15 January 1986. The event was inaugurated by [[Abdus Salam]].<ref>{{cite web|title=6 biotechnology institutes to be set up", Aligarh news.jpg|date=29 December 2023 |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/The-Times-of-India}} published 16 Jan 1986</ref> He performed a critical role toward the establishment of the Interdisciplinary Biotechnology Institute for Modern Biological and Biotechnological Education at Aligarh along with the AMU administration in 1984.<ref>{{cite news |title=Acceptance of alternative ways of thinking and mutual respect are "India's natural way of life": President Kovind |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/acceptance-of-alternative-ways-of-thinking-and-mutual-respect-are-india-s-natural-way-of-life-president-kovind-118030700728_1.html |access-date=4 September 2022 |publisher=Business Standard |date=7 March 2018}}</ref><ref name="our publication1">{{cite news |title=The last session was dedicated to Late Prof Ahmad Salahuddin, Founder Director, IBU as Professor A Salahuddin Oration |url=https://old.amu.ac.in/about3.jsp?did=3986 |access-date=4 September 2022 |agency=AMU News |publisher=Aligarh Muslim University |date=3 January 2019}}</ref>

==Research==
Egg white [[ovalbumin]]: The unfolding of ovalbumin, a 45 kDa protein, as a function of guanidine hydrochloride (0-6M) occurred reversibly in one step. The protein fractions in native (N) and the denatured states (D) were characterized by UV spectrometry and viscosity measurements at defined temperatures in buffer pH 7.0. The thermodynamics of folding and possibly kinetics followed a two state transition (N->D). The data were consistent with the fact that the native state was stabilized by [[hydrophobic effect]] in aqueous solution; this effect was diminished by introducing Guanidine hydrochloride to protein solution with concomitant transition to denatured state, [[random coil]] conformation similar to a nascent polypeptide chain.<ref>{{cite journal |author=F. Ahmad |author2=A. Salahuddin|title=Reversible unfolding of the major fraction of ovalbumin by guanidine hydrochloride|journal=Biochemistry|volume=15|issue=23|pages=5168–5175|year=1976|doi=10.1021/bi00668a034|pmid=4855653}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=The native and denatured states of ovalbumin|vauthors=Ansari AA, Ahmad R, Salahuddin A |journal= Biochemical Journal|volume=126|issue=2|pages=447–8|year=1972|doi=10.1042/bj1260447|pmid=501085|pmc=1178394 }}</ref>

Egg white [[Ovomucoid]]: The unfolding of ovomucoid (N), a domain containing 28 kDa protein, by guanidine hydrochloride did not proceed in a single step but occurred in two steps; the transition at low denaturant was associated with an intermediate, native-like, structure (X), and at high denaturant, protein existed in random coil structure (D). The reversible unfolding at each step (N->X->D) followed a two state transition pattern, albeit with somewhat different folding rates for the intermediate and native structures (1978).<ref>{{cite journal|author= Baig MA. and Salahuddin A.|title=Occurrence and characterization of stable intermediate state(s) in the unfolding of ovomucoid by guanidine Hydrochloride|journal= Biochemical Journal|volume=171|issue=1|pages=89–97|year=1978|doi=10.1042/bj1710089 |pmid=646827 |pmc=1184137}}</ref> The studies in his lab indicated that in vivo protein folding may not be explained by the amino acid sequence of an individual protein alone. Independently, the molecular biology of [[Chaperone (protein)|chaperones]] succeeded in the identification of additional folding factors in 1989.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Goloubinoff P, Christeller JT, Gatenby AA, Lorimer GH | title = Reconstitution of active dimeric ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase from an unfolded state depends on two chaperonin proteins and Mg-ATP | journal = Nature | volume = 342 | issue = 6252 | pages = 884–9 | year = 1989 | pmid = 10532860 | doi = 10.1038/342884a0 | bibcode = 1989Natur.342..884G | s2cid = 4319510 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |vauthors = Levinthal C| title =Are there pathways for protein folding?| journal =Journal de Chimie Physique | volume = 65 | pages = 44–45 | year = 1968 | doi = 10.1051/jcp/1968650044 | bibcode =1968JCP....65...44L}}</ref> The latter studies marked the beginning of modern protein folding with manipulation in human health.

==Awards and honours==
Salahuddin was President of Society of Biological Chemists SBC (India) from 1989 to 1990;<ref>Ahmad Salahuddin{{cite web|title=Society of Biological Chemists (India)(1930–2011)|page=16|url=http://sbcihq.in/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/sbc-rules-79-Book.pdf}} retrieved 31 July 2023</ref> a Member of the editorial board of [[Indian Journal of Biochemistry and Biophysics]](1985–1988); Visiting Associate Professor, [[University of Maryland]] 1975;<ref>{{cite journal|author1= A. Salahuddin and E. Bucci|title=Conformational aspects of the interaction of polyanions with ligended beta chains of human hemoglobin|journal= Biochemistry|volume=15|pages=3399–3405|year=1976|issue=16 |doi=10.1021/bi00661a001|pmid=952864 }}</ref> Member of Protein Society, Bethesda, USA(1995–1997); Member of the [[New York Academy of Science]], New York(1995–1996); Member of the executive committee of the Society of Biological Chemists, India(1974–1975); Member of the executive committee of Indian [[Biophysical Society]], India (1991–1993); Member of the [[Guha Research Conference]], India (1987–1992); and Member of [[Sigma Xi]] (USA).<ref>Ahmad Salahuddin{{cite web|url=https://www.sigmaxi.org/members/member-directory?fn=Ahmad&ln=Salahuddin&disc=0&chap=Duke%20University&match=True|title=Sigma Xi Member Directory}} retrieved 31 July 2023</ref>

==Death==
Salahuddin died on 29 November 1996 at the age of 59 after a difficult illness. Eulogies by his former students were read at the annual meeting of the Aligarh Alumni Association Washington DC;<ref>{{cite web|title=Annual meeting of the Aligarh Alumni Association, Washington DC.jpg|url=http://www.aligarhdc.org/home/}} published 4 July 1997</ref>
by others at a session at AMU Aligarh on 3 Jan 2019.<ref name="our publication1"/> At his death he was survived by his wife and two daughters.
